shell.nodeIpTip: The node's static IP — this is the OTA target. It comes from the backend config, not telemetry.
shell.noBrokerTitle: No connection to the MQTT broker.

ota.title: OTA session

env.productionHint: LOG_LEVEL=0 — the one that goes to the field
env.developmentHint: LOG_LEVEL=2 — costs 2 s of delay per wake

ota.intro: Publishes {"cmd":"maintenance"} retained. The node picks it up on its next wake, brings up ArduinoOTA and announces it on the status topic — no need to ping it.
ota.timeoutHint: The firmware caps this at 60 min (SERVICE_MODE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MIN). During the session the node stays awake at 50-140 mA with no deep sleep.
ota.unsafeTitle: Battery at {{volts}} V — flashing is not advisable.
ota.override: I understand the risk, arm anyway
ota.unknownRisk: No battery reading yet — it arrives with the first telemetry cycle, within 60 s. If it's better to wait, the warning will show up on its own.
ota.noBroker: No connection to the MQTT broker.
ota.waitingTitle: Waiting for the node to wake up
ota.wakingNow: The node should be waking up right now
ota.stillRetained: · the command stays retained until it reads it
ota.replacesPing: This replaces the old ping window: the node publishes service_mode_active when ArduinoOTA is up, which is the real signal that it's ready to flash.
ota.restartsTitle: The node restarted the session {{count}} times.
ota.restartsBody: It loses MQTT partway through, goes to sleep unable to clear the retained command, and reads it again on waking. With firmware ≤ 1.1.0 each restart gets a brand new full timeout. The backend still cuts it off at {{min}} min from when it was armed — if the flash doesn't fit in that window, arm it again.
ota.devWarning: The development build burns a fixed 2 s in delay(2000) on every wake, at 50-140 mA. Don't leave it in the field longer than necessary.
ota.runFrom: Run it from weather-station-station-iot/. When it's done, the node reboots, re-enters service mode on its own (it's flagged in RTC memory) and publishes its new version — that's when this view verifies it automatically.
ota.flashedNote: The version changed, so the OTA went through. Deactivate so it returns to its normal cycle: otherwise it stays awake until the timeout runs out.

toast.deactivated: Service mode deactivated — the node returns to its normal cycle

battery.title: Battery
battery.noReading: No reading yet — waiting for the first telemetry cycle.
battery.voltsTipHeartbeat: Measured with the node awake in service mode, i.e. under load. This is the number that matters for deciding whether to start a flash.
battery.voltsTipTelemetry: Measured on the latest telemetry cycle, with WiFi active. It reads a bit below resting voltage, which is the safe side to be wrong on.
battery.socTip: SoC comes from a piecewise Li-ion curve, not a straight line: the discharge is very flat between 3.7 and 4.0 V. The tiers come from componentes_y_conexiones.md and describe which rails the firmware should shed — not implemented yet, so here they are just a label.
battery.panelTip: Reading from the panel's INA219. Below 20 mA is considered no significant charge: a few mA is leakage or the MPPT clipping on a nearly full battery, not real charging.

risk.safeTip: Above 4.00 V. The threshold is deliberately stricter than the power tiers: during service mode the node stays awake with no deep sleep to let the voltage recover.
risk.cautionTip: Between 3.85 and 4.00 V. Enough for a short session, but avoid repeated flashes: each one keeps the node awake at 50-140 mA and sags the voltage a bit further.
risk.unsafeTip: Below 3.85 V. The risk isn't running out of capacity —15 min at ~100 mA is ~25 mAh out of 1500— it's sag under load: the boost converter pulls more input current as Vin falls, which feeds back into the drop until a brownout mid-write.

battery.trendTitle: Trend — a single instantaneous reading can't tell "it's recovering" from "it's been dropping for three days"

health.title: Node health

state.service_modeTip: The node is awake with ArduinoOTA listening. During the session it does not publish telemetry, only heartbeats every 30 s — that's why "last seen" switches to counting against the heartbeat.
state.sleepingTip: The node sleeps and wakes on its duty cycle to measure, publish and go back to sleep. Between wakes it is not reachable over the network: flashing requires activating service mode.
state.overdueTip: A full cycle plus the connection margin has passed with no telemetry arriving. Usually the node woke up but failed to connect to WiFi or MQTT on that wake, so it went back to sleep without publishing. One isolated cycle is normal with marginal signal; several in a row is not.
state.unknownTip: No message from the node has arrived yet since the backend started. If this persists for more than a minute, check the connection to the broker.

health.debugTip: LOG_LEVEL=2: setup() burns a fixed 2 s in delay(2000) on every wake, at 50-140 mA, with no benefit in the field. Reflash with ota_production.
health.bootCountTip: Wake counter stored in RTC memory. It increments at the start of setup(), before networking, so a jump means the node woke up but did not get to publish. Resets to zero on reflash or on power loss.
health.rssiTip: WiFi signal strength as seen by the node. Above -70 dBm the link is healthy; near -80 it becomes marginal and wakes that fail to publish start showing up.
health.countdownTipFuture: Countdown to the next expected message, every {{sec}} s. If it reaches zero and keeps dropping, the node did not show up when it should have.
health.countdownTipPast: The node should have published {{sec}} s ago. A short delay is normal —the wake takes a few seconds to connect— but if it keeps growing, that cycle was lost.
health.payloadTip: Usable bytes of the PubSubClient buffer: 768 minus the header and the topic name. If the payload doesn't fit, the whole publish is silently dropped — it has already happened on sub-zero early mornings, when every negative temperature adds a digit.
health.sensorTipDht: dht11_ok field in the JSON. The physical sensor has been a DHT22 since 2026-07-25; the name was kept so as not to split the historical series in InfluxDB.
health.hideExpectedTip: Hides reboots that explain themselves —a reboot you requested, a reflash— to leave only what deserves attention.
health.noneUnexplained: None unexplained. All discontinuities come from a reboot or a reflash.
health.heartbeatVoltageNote: The voltage shown comes from the service mode heartbeat, i.e. measured with the node awake and draining.

live.title: Live mode
live.intro: The node stops sleeping and publishes every ~{{sec}}s instead of every 60. Only worth it while the charger is already rejecting energy: <0>~53 mAh per hour, against ~47 mAh for a full day of the normal cycle.
live.costTip: Measured over a 47 min field session: 53.1 mA sustained, 41.3 mAh consumed. The normal duty cycle uses about 47 mAh for a whole day, so an hour of live mode costs roughly a day of ordinary operation.

exitReason.low_battery: the pack dropped below its floor
exitReason.budget_exhausted: no budget was left from earlier sessions

live.floorCooldown: The node judged conditions from its own sensors, so automatic arming stands down for an hour.
live.otherCommandBody: The node has a single command slot and every mode reads an empty payload as “stop”, so they cannot be queued against each other. Clear that one first.
live.forceTip: Skips only the node's panel-voltage floor, so the mode can be exercised without sun. The node caps a forced session at {{min}} min, and the pack floor, the budget and the broker floor all still apply.
live.footer: The node exits on its own when the panel, the pack, the budget or the broker say so — nothing here can leave it awake indefinitely.

payloads.title: Broker payloads
payloads.noMessages: No messages yet. The node publishes telemetry on its normal cycle.
payloads.backlogNote: On connect, the backend delivers what it had stored. It's the MQTT client and always runs, with or without a browser open.
payloads.backlogDivider: everything above already happened — the backend stored it while no one was watching

toast.emptyPayload: The payload is empty — it is a cleared retained message.

console.title: Command console
console.subtitle: The node reads the retained topic on wake, so a command waits until the next cycle
console.footer: Published with retain. The backend validates that it's JSON — parseCommand() discards anything that isn't, and the node would just continue its normal cycle without any warning.

log.title: Node logs
log.intro: Capturing runs during normal cycles and costs no energy. Transferring is the only part that needs the node awake, which is why it's a separate step.
log.unsupportedTitle: The backend does not expose the logging system yet.
log.unsupportedBody: This panel needs the logs field in the state snapshot. Rebuild and redeploy the backend image; the node's firmware also needs to be on 1.3.0 or newer.

level.1blurb: Only failures: WiFi, MQTT and publish. A healthy cycle writes nothing.
level.2blurb: One line per cycle stage, plus anomalies. This is the one that answers "WiFi or MQTT?".
level.3blurb: Every WiFi attempt individually. For when level 2 is not enough.

log.dictCachedTip: The backend already has the code→text dictionary for this firmware version cached, so there's no need to ask the node for it on the next transfer.
log.memoryFull: full — already overwriting the oldest events
log.capturingSinceTip: When the window the node currently has stored started. It resets on a level change and on transfer, because in both cases the node empties its memory. The backend derives it by watching telemetry —the node has no clock— so it has the precision of one cycle.
log.runningSinceBeforeTip: The backend found the capture already running —it restarted after the capture started— so it doesn't know when it really began. The number is a floor: it could have been running for much longer.
log.levelButtonTip: Level {{level}}. {{blurb}} Lasts {{window}} before it starts overwriting the oldest events.
log.levelHint: Level {{level}}: {{blurb}} The estimated window assumes {{sec}} s cycles. Capture memory lives in the ESP32's RTC memory and cannot be grown: more detail means fewer hours.
log.levelMismatch: The node is capturing at {{current}}. Starting again switches it to {{next}} and discards what has been captured so far.
log.startTip: Publishes the command on the retained topic. The node picks it up on waking (up to one cycle of delay) and starts from zero: anything captured before is discarded.
log.stopTip: Stops the capture and empties the node's memory. Any events not yet transferred are lost — transfer first if that matters.
log.pendingPickedUp: The node picked up the command and is applying it. The telemetry that confirms it is still needed, which comes in this same cycle.
log.pendingRetained: The command stayed retained on the broker. The node only reads it on waking{{when}}, and until then it keeps capturing as it was. If the cycle fails to publish —which happens often— confirmation is delayed until the next one.
log.lockedTitle: Capture cannot be changed while the node is in service mode.
log.lockedInService: During the session the node ignores everything that arrives on the command topic except the request to exit, and closing the session clears the topic — so the command would not be delayed, it would be lost.
log.lockedArmed: There is a retained maintenance command waiting for the node to wake up. The topic holds only one message, so publishing the capture command here would overwrite it and cancel service mode.
log.lockedTail: Transferring still works. To change the capture, exit service mode and wait for the next normal cycle.

confirm.startTitle: Starting discards the capture in progress
confirm.startBody: There is an active capture at {{level}}. Starting a new one erases it and starts from zero.
confirm.stopBody: On stopping, the node empties its capture memory.
confirm.transferFirstStart: If they matter, cancel and use Transfer logs from the node first.
confirm.transferFirstStop: If they matter, cancel and use Transfer logs from the node first — that leaves the memory empty and the capture stopped, which is the same thing you were after.
confirm.reportedLost_one: The node reported {{count}} event in its last telemetry — if you haven't transferred it, it will be lost. The number can be up to one cycle behind, so there could be more.
confirm.reportedLost_other: The node reported {{count}} events in its last telemetry — if you haven't transferred them, they will be lost. The number can be up to one cycle behind, so there could be more.
confirm.reportedNone_one: The node reported {{count}} event in its last telemetry. The number can be up to one cycle behind, so there could be more.
confirm.reportedNone_other: The node reported {{count}} events in its last telemetry. The number can be up to one cycle behind, so there could be more.

log.needsWakeTitle: The node needs to be woken up first.
log.needsWakeBody: Outside a service mode session the node sleeps almost the whole cycle and doesn't listen to the request topic, so it can't respond to a transfer. The capture keeps running fine in the meantime.
log.armTip: Publishes the maintenance command with the default 15 min timeout. The node picks it up on its next wake and stays awake — only then can it be transferred.
log.armAlreadyRequested: Service mode already requested — waiting on the node
log.transferTip: Fetches the captured events page by page. The node only clears them after the backend confirms they all arrived, so an interrupted transfer doesn't cost the capture.
log.keepTip: Fetches a copy without stopping the capture or emptying the node's memory, for investigations that are still ongoing. By default the transfer empties and stops it.
log.exportJsonTip: Downloads the capture as JSON, with the code dictionary and time anchors included. Stays readable even after the firmware moves on and renumbers the codes.
log.exportNdjsonTip: Same as the JSON but one event per line, with a header line first. Same format as the payload viewer's export.
log.clearedKept: The node's memory was cleared but the capture is still active.
log.clearedStopped: The node cleared its memory and stopped the capture.
log.notCleared: The node did not confirm the clear: the capture is still occupying its memory.
log.filterPlaceholder: Filter by text — e.g. rssi, timeout, mqtt
log.estimatedTimeTip: Estimated time: this cycle did not publish telemetry, so it was interpolated from the nearest cycle with a real timestamp using the measured awake time. The deep sleep timer has ±5% drift, so the deviation grows with distance.

toast.stopped: The node stopped the capture and cleared its memory.
toast.notConfirmed: The node did not confirm the capture change. The command is still retained: if the node shows up, it will apply it — check the status chip in a couple of cycles.
toast.noEvents: The node had no captured events.

log.droppedBody_one: The node's memory filled up and overwrote {{count}} event with a newer one, so the capture doesn't reach back to the start of the window and may not cover what you were looking for. Next time, a leaner level lasts longer.
log.droppedBody_other: The node's memory filled up and overwrote {{count}} events with newer ones, so the capture doesn't reach back to the start of the window and may not cover what you were looking for. Next time, a leaner level lasts longer.
